subtitleEn: Follow a talk with a teacher, line by line.
hoyaIntroEn: Listen to each line and follow along. Let's ask about new words!

quests.blurbEn: Ask the teacher what something is, and who.

steps.hoyaLineEn: A new word! Let's ask the teacher what it is.

pages.captionEn: Point at a thing and ask what it is. The answer names it.
For a person, ask who it is instead.

steps.hoyaLineEn: You asked what and who. You read along so well!

replies.whyEn: That asks about a person. The teacher is holding up a thing, so say what it is.
That is a greeting. The teacher asked a question, so answer it.
That names a person. This one is a thing, so name the thing.
That names a thing. The teacher asks who it is, so name a person.
That asks a question back. The teacher is asking you, so give an answer.
That names a thing. The teacher asks who, so name a person.
That names a thing. The teacher asks who, so name a person.

nodes.closingEn: You told the teacher what each thing is and who each person is!

quests.blurbEn: Ask where things are at school.
quests.teaserEn: Next: a whole talk, from hello to thank you.

steps.hoyaLineEn: Where is everything at school? Let's ask!

pages.captionEn: Name the place or the thing, then ask where it is.
The answer can be short: here, or over there.

steps.hoyaLineEn: You asked where things are. Now you know the way!

replies.whyEn: That says what it is. The teacher asks where it is, so say here or over there.
That asks who someone is. The teacher asks where the bag is.
That names a person. The teacher asks where the book is.
That says what it is. Say where it is: here or over there.
That asks what something is. The teacher asks where the eraser is.
That is a greeting. Answer the question: say where the eraser is.
That names a thing. The teacher asks where the restroom is.
That asks who someone is. The teacher asks where the restroom is.

nodes.closingEn: You said where each one is!

quests.blurbEn: Follow a whole talk: hello, a question, an answer, thanks.

steps.hoyaLineEn: Let's follow a whole talk with the teacher, line by line.

pages.captionEn: A talk can start with hello, then a question.
After the answer, say thank you.

steps.hoyaLineEn: You followed a whole talk, from hello to thank you!

replies.whyEn: That is a thank-you. The teacher said hello first, so greet the teacher back.
That says where something is. Greet the teacher back first.
You have already said hello. The teacher answered you, so say thank you.
That asks who someone is. The teacher answered your question, so say thank you.
The pencil is right here. The teacher is giving it to you, so say thank you.
That tells your name. The teacher is handing you a pencil, so say thank you.
You have already said thank you. The teacher asks what it is, so name it.
You have already said hello. Tell the teacher what it is.

nodes.closingEn: You followed a whole talk, from hello to thank you!

culture.textEn: Hangeul Day, {ko:한글날}, is on 9 October. It celebrates the making of Hunminjeongeum, the letters now called Hangeul, and the day they were shared with everyone.

sources.title: 한글날이 10월 9일인 이유는?
sources.quoteOrLocator: ‘한글날은 세종대왕이 창제한 훈민정음의 반포를 기념하고, 한글의 연구와 보급을 장려하기 위해 정한 날이다. 현재 한글날(10월 9일)은 … 5대 국경일 중 하나’ / ‘‘백성을 가르치는 바른 소리’라는 의미를 가진 ‘훈민정음(訓民正音)’은 … 하나는 1443년 세종대왕이 만든 우리의 문자를 가리키는 것이고, 다른 하나는 이 문자에 대해 풀이하여 1446년에 간행한 책을 가리키는 것이다.’

sources.title: 한글날 (한국세시풍속사전)
sources.publisher: 국립민속박물관 (National Folk Museum of Korea) — 한국민속대백과사전
sources.quoteOrLocator: 정의: ‘훈민정음(訓民正音) 곧 오늘의 한글을 창제해서 세상에 펴낸 것을 기념하고, 우리 글자 한글의 우수성을 기리기 위한 국경일.’ / ‘광복 후 양력 10월 9일로 확정되었으며’ 유래: ‘훈민정음은 세종대왕 25년 곧 서기 1443년에 완성하여 3년 동안의 시험 기간을 거쳐 세종 28년인 서기 1446년에 세상에 반포되었다.’

verification.notes:
Pass 1 (author sourcing, CM-3C, 2026-10-23): the National Hangeul Museum webzine article 한글날이 10월 9일인 이유는? (2018, no. 63) says Hangeul Day, 9 October, marks the publication of 훈민정음 and is one of the five national days; the National Folk Museum of Korea entry 한글날 (Encyclopedia of Korean Seasonal Customs, topic 5230) defines it as the national day that marks the making and publishing of 훈민정음, today's 한글, and says the date was fixed at 9 October (solar) after liberation, from the 1446 publication. English paraphrase.
Pass 2 (fact check, 2026-10-23): entry fetched again; 10월 9일, 창제 and 세상에 펴낸 found. 'Shared with everyone' paraphrases 세상에 펴낸/반포. Claim holds.
Pass 3 (MAR checklist pass by the authoring agent, 2026-10-23): F-CURR-002 §5.1 conventions (institution named as on the access date, no UNESCO claim beyond the exact element, shared East Asian heritage not framed as Korean in origin), §7.7 checklist (no age wording, no emoji, no speaking UI, neutral tone) and the 해요체 of the tokens checked. Pass. The independent MAR culture review re-runs in the PR review stage.
Pass 4 (independent MAR culture, facts and language review, a reviewer agent other than the author, 2026-10-23): National Hangeul Museum webzine (hangeul.go.kr) and NFM 한글날 (5230) re-read: 9 October, marks the making and publishing of 훈민정음, today's 한글. Holds. es/ko checked.

culture.textEn: King Sejong finished the new letters in 1443. In 1446 they were made public in a book named Hunminjeongeum, which means the right sounds to teach the people.

sources.title: 한글날이 10월 9일인 이유는?
sources.quoteOrLocator: ‘한글날은 세종대왕이 창제한 훈민정음의 반포를 기념하고, 한글의 연구와 보급을 장려하기 위해 정한 날이다. 현재 한글날(10월 9일)은 … 5대 국경일 중 하나’ / ‘‘백성을 가르치는 바른 소리’라는 의미를 가진 ‘훈민정음(訓民正音)’은 … 하나는 1443년 세종대왕이 만든 우리의 문자를 가리키는 것이고, 다른 하나는 이 문자에 대해 풀이하여 1446년에 간행한 책을 가리키는 것이다.’

sources.title: 한글날 (한국세시풍속사전)
sources.publisher: 국립민속박물관 (National Folk Museum of Korea) — 한국민속대백과사전
sources.quoteOrLocator: 정의: ‘훈민정음(訓民正音) 곧 오늘의 한글을 창제해서 세상에 펴낸 것을 기념하고, 우리 글자 한글의 우수성을 기리기 위한 국경일.’ / ‘광복 후 양력 10월 9일로 확정되었으며’ 유래: ‘훈민정음은 세종대왕 25년 곧 서기 1443년에 완성하여 3년 동안의 시험 기간을 거쳐 세종 28년인 서기 1446년에 세상에 반포되었다.’

sources.title: Hunminjeongum Manuscript
sources.quoteOrLocator: ‘The manuscript published in the ninth lunar month of 1446, contains the promulgation by Sejong the Great … of the Korean alphabet of the same name, now called han-gul, the development of which he completed in 1443.’ / ‘Registration Year: 1997’

verification.notes:
Pass 1 (author sourcing, CM-3C, 2026-10-23): the National Hangeul Museum article 한글날이 10월 9일인 이유는? says 훈민정음 means ‘the right sounds to teach the people’, names the letters Sejong made in 1443 and the book that explains them, published in 1446; the National Folk Museum of Korea entry 한글날 (유래) says 훈민정음 was completed in 1443 and made public in 1446; the UNESCO Memory of the World page says Sejong completed the alphabet in 1443 and the manuscript was published in the ninth lunar month of 1446. Same years as the reviewed card:hangeul back. English paraphrase.
Pass 2 (fact check, 2026-10-23): both pages fetched again; 1443 and 1446 found in both. Claim holds.
Pass 3 (MAR checklist pass by the authoring agent, 2026-10-23): F-CURR-002 §5.1 conventions (institution named as on the access date, no UNESCO claim beyond the exact element, shared East Asian heritage not framed as Korean in origin), §7.7 checklist (no age wording, no emoji, no speaking UI, neutral tone) and the 해요체 of the tokens checked. Pass. The independent MAR culture review re-runs in the PR review stage.
Pass 4 (independent MAR culture, facts and language review, a reviewer agent other than the author, 2026-10-23): National Hangeul Museum: 1443 the script, 1446 the book, 백성을 가르치는 바른 소리; NFM 5230: completed 1443, published 1446; UNESCO page: completed in 1443, published 1446. Holds. es/ko checked.

culture.textEn: The 1446 book that explains the letters was inscribed in UNESCO's Memory of the World Register in 1997, as the Hunminjeongum Manuscript.

sources.title: Hunminjeongum Manuscript
sources.quoteOrLocator: ‘The manuscript published in the ninth lunar month of 1446, contains the promulgation by Sejong the Great … of the Korean alphabet of the same name, now called han-gul, the development of which he completed in 1443.’ / ‘Registration Year: 1997’

sources.title: 한글날 (한국세시풍속사전)
sources.publisher: 국립민속박물관 (National Folk Museum of Korea) — 한국민속대백과사전
sources.quoteOrLocator: 정의: ‘훈민정음(訓民正音) 곧 오늘의 한글을 창제해서 세상에 펴낸 것을 기념하고, 우리 글자 한글의 우수성을 기리기 위한 국경일.’ / ‘광복 후 양력 10월 9일로 확정되었으며’ 유래: ‘훈민정음은 세종대왕 25년 곧 서기 1443년에 완성하여 3년 동안의 시험 기간을 거쳐 세종 28년인 서기 1446년에 세상에 반포되었다.’

verification.notes:
Pass 1 (author sourcing, CM-3C, 2026-10-23): the UNESCO Memory of the World page 'Hunminjeongum Manuscript' gives the 1446 manuscript with its commentaries and 'Registration Year: 1997'; the National Folk Museum of Korea entry 한글날 says the book was registered in the Memory of the World in October 1997. The UNESCO claim names the exact element under its UNESCO name (§5.1), the book, not the alphabet.
Pass 2 (fact check, 2026-10-23): both pages fetched again; the element name and 1997 found. Claim holds.
Pass 3 (MAR checklist pass by the authoring agent, 2026-10-23): F-CURR-002 §5.1 conventions (institution named as on the access date, no UNESCO claim beyond the exact element, shared East Asian heritage not framed as Korean in origin), §7.7 checklist (no age wording, no emoji, no speaking UI, neutral tone) and the 해요체 of the tokens checked. Pass. The independent MAR culture review re-runs in the PR review stage.
Pass 4 (independent MAR culture, facts and language review, a reviewer agent other than the author, 2026-10-23): UNESCO Memory of the World page re-read: the element is named Hunminjeongum Manuscript, inscribed 1997, the 1446 book with the proclamation and commentaries; the note uses 'inscribed' and the exact UNESCO name only (§5.1). NFM 5230 agrees (1997). Holds. es/ko checked.

notes: Language pass 4 (MAR): spelling, spacing, register and romanization clean; applied the one-order Story Sequences, Hoya greeting the teacher back in q3, the ko q3 title on the taught thank-you, Let's in Hoya lines, es Siguiente, plainer ko glosses; kept 연필 여기 있어요 (natural colloquial order).

Culture pass 5 (MAR): no culture claim, so no sources; school etiquette fixed (the pupil returns the greeting); cast is Hoya and an unnamed teacher (선생님 / Teacher / Docente), addressed by title as pupils do; no real person, brand or price; no age wording.

CM-3C (F-CURR-002 §5.2 S4, 2026-10-23): culture notes n1-n3 added (Hangeul Day on 9 October, Hunminjeongeum 1443/1446, the Hunminjeongum Manuscript in Memory of the World 1997), sources National Folk Museum of Korea and UNESCO, each with its own verification record.

Culture notes (CM-3C, MAR 2026-10-23): an independent reviewer agent re-read every source of the new notes (all §6.6 hosts, the allowlisted one first), checked §5.1 and §7.7 and the es and ko overlays; findings applied. No native-speaker or expert review is claimed.

Check rotation MAR (row CM-3A S4, F-CURR-002 section 7.1, 2026-10-27; passes: language, culture and facts, learning design, reviser, third pass): Letters plays Tap to Respond and Role Play (a teacher at school, 4 turns, every branch ends well, an amber nudge and a retry on a less natural reply); the Checks are Cloze Pick, Sentence Builder and Cloze Pick, each a produce round.

CM-3A S4 MAR (cont.): Language: 해요체 throughout; the pupil greets the teacher back and thanks with 감사합니다; tiles are taught nouns read by their meaning (할머니, 연필), and no distractor shows the teacher with 있어요 in place of the honorific 계세요 (NIKL 표준 언어 예절). Culture and facts: no new claim; the CM-3C notes are unchanged.

CM-3A S4 MAR (cont.): Learning design: every Role Play turn and Check re-asks an exchange or sentence the cell teaches, so Stage 4 teaches no more review items than before (section 4.3 gate). Reviser and third pass: es and ko glosses and why lines checked against the cell overlays. No native-speaker or expert review is claimed.
